findings.explanation: 1 cookie(s) classified as requiring consent were stored before any interaction with the page: _fbp (Meta (Facebook) Pixel, marketing, first-party). Art. 5(3) requires prior consent for storing information on the visitor's device unless it is strictly necessary for a service the visitor requested.
No request to a known analytics or advertising service, and no unclassified beacon-like request, was observed before any interaction. No third-party site was contacted.
No localStorage or sessionStorage key associated with analytics or advertising was written before any interaction. No Web Storage key was written.
A consent interface was detected on the page (unidentified platform; controls recognised: accept, settings).

The first layer of the consent interface offers acceptance (“Accepter & fermer”) but no refusal option was found; other controls: “Paramétrer” (settings). The CNIL strongly recommends that refusing be possible on the same screen and as easily as accepting, and most authorities in the EDPB Cookie Banner Taskforce considered a banner with no refusal option on any layer to be an infringement.
No analytics cookie was stored before consent, so no audience-measurement lifetime applies to this observation.
This point cannot be established by observing the website from outside. It is listed so a reviewer can examine it.
